title: Compatible germ-semilinear evaluations descend uniquely to a linear stalk map
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, $x\in X$, $\mathcal O$ a presheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal P$ a presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules: its sections are $\mathcal O(U)$-modules and its restriction maps are additive and semilinear over the ring restrictions. Write $\mathcal O_x$ and $\mathcal P_x$ for their stalks, with germs $r_x$ and $s_x$ and the germ scalar action of [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]. Let $A$ be an $\mathcal O_x$-module. For every open neighbourhood $U$ of $x$, suppose an additive map $e_U:\mathcal P(U)\to A$ is given, with $e_U(rs)=r_xe_U(s)$ for all $r\in\mathcal O(U)$ and $s\in\mathcal P(U)$. Assume $e_V(s|_V)=e_U(s)$ whenever $x\in V\subseteq U$. Then there exists a unique $\mathcal O_x$-linear map $\overline e:\mathcal P_x\to A$ satisfying $\overline e(s_x)=e_U(s)$ for every $U\ni x$ and $s\in\mathcal P(U)$. No sheaf condition on either presheaf is required.
